study_identification.author_journal_year: Verdi S, et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia, 2024
study_identification.title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: To apply neuroanatomical normative modeling to serial MRI data to quantify regional changes in brain structure as AD progresses, and to assess whether these markers can track disease trajectories, predict progression from MCI to AD, and relate to other AD markers.

dataset_name.answer: Reference: OASIS, ABCD, UKB; Research: ADNI

quality_checking_detail.answer: Reference: manual and automated filtering; Research: visual review

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: A non-Gaussian Bayesian regression model was implemented, which accounts for the non-Gaussian distributions of the cortical thickness andsubcortical volume data and adjusts for unwanted noise from scanning acquisition across multiple sites. The distribution parameters of the reference normative model were calibrated to our ADNI dataset using 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site, with the aim of reducing site effects and software version effects (i.e., FreeSurfer v5 or v6).

model_origin_detail.answer: Trained on 58,836 scans from 82 sites. Available at https://github.com/predictive-clinical-neuroscience/braincharts.

predictor_effects.answer: Mixed-effects model with site handled by Bayesian regression and calibration.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used a non-Gaussian Bayesian regression model that explicitly accounts for site effects. It also performs a calibration step to adapt the model to the specific test data (ADNI), further reducing site and scanner effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: A non-Gaussian Bayesian regression model was implemented, which accounts for the non-Gaussian distributions of the cortical thickness andsubcortical volume data and adjusts for unwanted noise from scanning acquisition across multiple sites. ... Next, these estimates were calibrated to our specific test data (i.e., ADNI), using an adapted transfer learning approach. The distribution parameters of the reference normative model were calibrated to our ADNI dataset using 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site, with the aim of reducing site effects and software version effects (i.e., FreeSurfer v5 or v6).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model is validated on a hold-out set of the same domain. 70% of the cognitively unimpaired controls from ADNI were used for calibration, and the remaining 30% were used for analysis, along with MCI and AD patients.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The distribution parameters of the reference normative model were calibrated to our ADNI dataset using 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site... The data from the remaining 30% of cognitively unimpaired controls, plus participants with MCI and patients with AD, were then compared to these normative models, generating z scores per region for each scan.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not mention validation on an independent dataset from the same domain (i.e., another longitudinal cohort of AD patients not from ADNI).

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention validation on a dataset from a different domain.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear models, linear mixed models, Cox proportional hazards regression, and linear regression were used to test for differences between diagnostic groups, to assess the rate of change in tOC, to predict progression from MCI to AD, and to examine the relationship between tOC and other cognitive, amyloid, and tau markers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individual patients' atrophy rates can be tracked by using regional outlier maps and total outlier count (tOC), which increase in AD and in people with MCI who convert to AD, and also correlate with multiple non-imaging markers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: tOC increased in AD and in people with MCI who converted to AD. A higher annual rate of change in tOC increased the risk of progression from MCI to AD. The hippocampus was identified as the region with the highest rate of change. The rate of change in tOC was associated with cognitive decline, amyloid and tau pathology, and APOE ε4 status.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The reference dataset is over-representative of European ancestry. The ADNI cohort is also predominantly of European ancestry and in the early to intermediate stages of AD. The use of different FreeSurfer versions might add noise. The model treats brain regions independently.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The authors suggest that normative modeling of serial scans could be used for early AD detection, for patient stratification in clinical trials, and as a personalized outcome measure.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive longitudinal analysis of normative modeling in AD, demonstrating its potential for tracking individual disease progression.
